title: Avoid surprising changes
summary: A function that returns a new value can be easier to reason about than one that changes its input. Make changes clear in the function name or contract.
introduction: A function that returns a new value can be easier to reason about than one that changes its input. Make changes clear in the function name or contract. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A function that returns a new value can be easier to reason about than one that changes its input. Make changes clear in the function name or contract.

blocks.title: Avoid surprising changes

blocks.text: The original stays 3,1,2; the copy becomes 1,2,3.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Use another list and compare both outputs.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: sort changes its array, so copy first when the caller expects the original to stay.
For more detail later, use this [Clean Code further reading](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/MDN/Writing_guidelines/Code_style_guide/JavaScript).
